status: In text.json (Fable, 2026-11-08, brief 102's sweep). `by: sky` lines are Sky's yes to Fable's sample ("yes - rewrites are much better"); `by: fable` lines are the sweep's hand edits to the same bar, for Sky's read on briefs/102/fable/sweep.html. The scenes and conversations are not in the style loop's families, so these have no loop score.

edits.speaker: fixer
edits.before: Could you do me a small favour? I can't pay.
edits.after: Could you do me a small favour? It's nothing much.
edits.why: "I can't pay" reads out what Ask means. Nobody asking a favour says so.

edits.speaker: driver
edits.before: Yes? Ask me straight and I'll listen.
edits.after: Yes? Be quick, I'm waiting on the Councillor.
edits.why: His opener told the player how to talk to him. Now he's a driver on duty, short with a stranger; the cards say what an Ask is.

edits.speaker: fixer
edits.before: A small favour, officer. Free of charge.
edits.after: Only a small favour, officer. Hear me out.
edits.why: "Free of charge" answered his joke by naming the Ask's price. She asks, as a person would.

edits.speaker: guard
edits.before: The patrol keeps to the yard. Nothing here for minutes.
edits.after: Quiet enough. The patrol's off round the yard.
edits.why: "Nothing here for minutes" timed the patrol for the player. He says what he sees; the Watch's chip carries the rounds.

edits.speaker: guard
edits.before: Five minutes. Then back on the steps.
edits.after: Just the one. Then back on the steps.
edits.why: Not in the offenders list: found on the way. A number in a person's mouth (Sky's rule on numbers in play), timing his break. Just the one coffee says he won't be long without a clock.

edits.speaker: clerk
edits.before: Mind the patrol, if you go round the back.
edits.after: Let's hope it stays that way.
edits.why: A clerk warning the guard about his own patrol was the player's tip in a clerk's mouth. Now they talk about the quiet day, which the player knows won't last.

edits.speaker: guard
edits.before: I know. It sweeps the yard.
edits.after: It will, while I'm on it.
edits.why: He explained the patrol's rounds. Now he's a guard sure of his door.

edits.speaker: guard
edits.before: Quiet on the door. The patrol is out in the yard.
edits.why: He told Inez, and the player, why the door was safe to leave. Now he's a man seeing someone in secret, uneasy to be seen with her.

edits.speaker: waitress
edits.after: Let them talk. Stay a while.
edits.why: Her answer to his new line, so the pair still talk to each other; no time in her mouth.

edits.speaker: waitress
edits.before: Then I'm with you. I watch that square all day, and if trouble's coming for you, I'll find a way to warn you.
edits.after: Then I'm with you. Whatever this is, please be careful.
edits.why: It announced a feature: helped, she warns the cell at the car. Unannounced, her shout of "Careful! Men by the car!" comes as a surprise that her kindness earned.

edits.speaker: guard
edits.before: Then my door's standing empty. Stay here, Inez.
edits.after: Stay inside, Inez. I'm getting back to that door.
edits.why: "My door's standing empty" spelled out the consequence. He says what he means to do now, and does it: he runs back to his door.

edits.speaker: driver
edits.before: The east yard. I'll give you a couple of minutes there, and then I drive on.
edits.after: The east yard. Fine, but I'll keep the engine running.
edits.why: One of the four lines Sky rejected ("none stays as it is"): it read out the bay's window. A nervous driver's own condition, a car man's detail; the Learned chip carries the wait.
